messages:
acme-pm: Hey team — hitting an issue with streaming responses from Redwood. When our client reconnects mid-stream the final chunk never arrives and the JSON is left open (clients see parse errors). Seen ~3:04pm UTC on us-west-2. Request ID: req_8f7a2b. Using edge proxy (Fastly) in front of your hosted API. Can share traces if useful.

maria: Thanks for the report — sorry about the break. Can you paste a minimal curl repro and the exact headers you send when reconnecting? Also confirm model/route and whether you use HTTP/2 or HTTP/1.1 to the Fastly edge.

acme-pm: Minimal repro below (we're using HTTP/2 between client and Fastly, then Fastly -> Redwood is HTTP/1.1):

```
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-open-8k","input":"stream test"}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```

When the user loses cellular and reconnects the client reopens the request; on reconnect the stream finishes but the last SSE event is missing the trailing "\n\n" and the JSON body is incomplete. We get a client-side parse error.

maria: Got it — assigning to Ken for deeper SRE/edge debugging. Ken, I've attached req_8f7a2b and a short pcap from the customer showing the reconnect pattern.

ken: Looking at the capture and our edge logs for req_8f7a2b. Pattern summary: 1) client connection drops (TCP FIN), 2) client opens a new connection to Fastly with same high-level request, 3) Fastly reuses the backend connection to Redwood and forwards remaining bytes. Observed symptom: the backend stream terminator (the SSE blank line after the final data: chunk) appears to be lost in the reassembly window. Sample stream we captured from the backend side:

```
data: {"id":"tok_123","choices":[{"delta":{"text":"..."},"finish_reason":null}]}
data: {"id":"tok_123","choices":[{"delta":{"text":"final token"}}]}
<socket close>  <-- missing final "\n\n" here
```

Client sees: `{"id":"tok_123","choices":[{"delta":{"text":"final token"}}]}` and then EOF -> JSON parse error.

ken: Quick hypothesis — when Fastly stitches backend responses across backend connection reuse, the very last CRLFCRLF boundary can be dropped if the backend emits it right as the underlying socket is torn down. On HTTP/2 this can also manifest as stream state reordering on certain proxies.

ken: Immediate mitigations to try (from support side):
- Ask client to send `Connection: close` on reconnect attempts so Fastly doesn't attempt to multiplex/reuse backend sockets for that connection.
- If using a custom edge, disable HTTP/2 multiplexing for the connection or force `Proxy-Connection: keep-alive` behavior that prevents premature backend reuse.
- Client-side: tolerate a trailing partial chunk by attempting a short reconnect and requesting the last ~256 bytes via a diagnostic route (we can add a debug tail API if you want).

maria: From Redwood side, we can also add a temporary server-side guard to always emit an explicit sentinel event at the very end of SSE streams (e.g. `data: __END_OF_STREAM__\n\n`) to make missing-final-chunk detection easier for clients. I can open a short-lived rollout for that if you want immediate protection while we work the proxy vendor.

acme-pm: Thanks — we can try the `Connection: close` workaround first. Also the sentinel event rollout sounds good to avoid crashing clients.

ken: For our postmortem/root cause analysis please send: full Fastly logs around the request (edge_request_id), the raw backend capture if possible, and any client-side reconnect timestamps. I've flagged this as P2 with networking team and will follow up with vendor (Fastly) — rough ETA 24–48h.

sre-bot: Auto-uploaded logs: s3://redwood-logs/support/1768129999/req_8f7a2b-edge.log (sanitized), backend_capture_req_8f7a2b.pcap.gz.

acme-pm: Appreciate the quick triage. We'll flip `Connection: close` on reconnects and report back within the hour.

maria: Perfect — keep us posted. If you run into other routes or different models exhibiting the same behavior include those request IDs so we can correlate. :thumbsup:
